sense: the working parts of a machine

evidence: Cic. N.D. 2.97: cum māchinātiōne quādam movērī aliquid vidēmus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: An artificial contrivance that makes a thing move; in Caesar also a machine or siege engine, and figuratively a trick, a machination (Lewis & Short), so the setting must make the mechanism clear.
The whole machine rather than its working parts (see machine); also a scheme or a trick (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: the way something works, a mechanism (of a process)
terms.comment: For the figurative sense, the way a process works: “the mechanism of the disease”. Built on ratiō with a gerund (see process).

phrases.latin: cum māchinātiōne quādam movērī aliquid vidēmus, ut sphaeram
phrases.english: when we see something moved by some mechanism, like a celestial globe

sources: Lewis & Short: machinatio · Lewis & Short: machina
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. mechanism.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 342.
